messages:
Lucia (Finance LATAM): Heads-up: vendor 'NorteData SA de CV' (MX) sent invoice INV-MX-334 for platform access and analytics. They charged 16% IVA (MXN). They attached an invoice PDF but no CFDI (timbrado) stamp visible. They asked Redwood to confirm if services are exported and eligible for tasa 0% (IVA 0%).

Marco (Tax US): Quick flags: Mexico requires electronic invoicing (CFDI) for tax purposes. For cross-border B2B services, IVA can be 0% if classified as exported services, but vendor must issue a CFDI with the correct tax treatment and the RFC (tax ID) and SAT stamp. If there's no CFDI, their tax treatment may be incorrect.

Lucia (Finance LATAM): The invoice shows RFC: NDE210923XXX and a line 'IVA 16%'. Bill-to is Redwood Inference LLC (US). They claim service delivered outside MX.

Nora (AP): From AP side we need: the CFDI XML/PDF with timbre fiscal (SAT stamp), the vendor RFC, and a clear tax breakdown line. If they claim tasa 0%, invoice must state 'exportación de servicios - tasa 0%'.

Diego (Payments): Also confirm bank account name matches their RFC/company name to avoid remediation. Currency is MXN; do we want to pay MXN or request USD?

Lucia (Finance LATAM): Drafting vendor message, pls review:```
Hola NorteData,

Gracias por el envío. To process payment we need the following documents:
1) The CFDI (electronically stamped invoice) XML/PDF with SAT timbre fiscal (UUID) and your RFC (NDE210923XXX) visible.
2) If you consider the supply an "exportación de servicios" (IVA tasa 0%), please re-issue the CFDI showing tasa 0% and reference the legal basis OR provide a short written confirmation of the place of supply.
3) Please confirm the exact legal name that appears on your RFC and the beneficiary bank account details for MXN remittance.

If you cannot provide a valid CFDI we may have to withhold the IVA or treat the tax as non-recoverable which could delay payment. Please upload docs to the vendor portal so AP can proceed.

Gracias,
Lucia (Finance LATAM)
```

Marco (Tax US): Add: "If you are not Mexican tax resident or believe different tax treatment applies, please provide supporting documentation (proof of foreign establishment or SAT guidance)."

Nora (AP): Add note: "Please attach the CFDI XML; PDFs alone sometimes miss the timbre info."

Lucia (Finance LATAM): Sent. Vendor reply: "We're MX-based and always charge IVA by default. We can re-issue with taux 0% only if you provide a certificate that services are consumed outside Mexico. We don't have that. Attached current invoice PDF and bank details."

Diego (Payments): That's awkward. They want us to provide a consumption certificate? Is that something finance issues?

Marco (Tax US): In practice we don't issue a "certificate of consumption". Usually vendor determines place-of-supply and issues correct CFDI. We can provide a written confirmation that the bill-to is Redwood Inference LLC (US) and where services are consumed, but vendor should re-issue. Recommend: 1) provide a short written statement confirming buyer is US entity and services used outside MX; 2) request reissued CFDI; 3) if they still charge IVA, accept charge for this invoice and classify as non-recoverable or seek refund via Mexican procedures (rare).

Lucia (Finance LATAM): Drafting quick note to vendor:```
Hi NorteData,

To help with CFDI re-issue, Redwood confirms the bill-to is Redwood Inference LLC, a US entity, and that the services will be consumed by our US team. Please re-issue the CFDI referencing "exportación de servicios" with tasa 0% if that is your legal basis. Otherwise please provide the stamped CFDI showing IVA charged so we can process payment.

Thanks,
Lucia (Finance LATAM)
```

NorteData SA de CV: Vendor: Thanks, we will consult our tax advisor and try to re-issue. If not, we'll keep the IVA on invoice and expect gross payment.

Nora (AP): If they insist on gross payment, we need written contractual gross-up or we'll pay net and they can reclaim IVA via Mexican channels. For now I'll hold payment pending CFDI or confirmation.

Diego (Payments): Putting invoice on hold and flagging for LATAM tax team. If they re-issue 0% CFDI we can proceed with payment in MXN.

Lucia (Finance LATAM): Noted. Action items: request CFDI XML, provide buyer consumption confirmation, escalate to tax counsel if vendor refuses to re-issue. Also update vendor onboarding checklist to request CFDI/RFC up front for Mexican suppliers. Closing thread for now. :white_check_mark:
